row_statement: Conjecture 15 of the arXiv version of Albert and Bouvel (for every n >= 3 the main cohort is larger than any other cohort of arch systems of size n) is false: at n = 78 the main cohort has exactly 33882709435158403490429948661355518 members (a Motzkin number), while another cohort, that of 74 nested arches around one arch holding three leaves, contains an explicit family of 34231997388422588678130382724372607 arch systems. Lean uses exactly the source's four rules, proves the main cohort's size by a counting recurrence, proves the witness lies outside the main cohort, and proves the lower bound by a bijection.

caveats: The authors already doubted the conjecture: the journal version keeps it only as 'tempting to formulate', says 'We are now inclined to believe that cohorts that are larger than the main cohort may exist even if this does not happen before a very large value of n', describes a failed attempt to build one, and asks to prove or disprove it. They gave no example. Describe the result as refuting the arXiv conjecture and answering the question the journal left open.

78 is not the first crossing: Opus found a different cohort that already beats the main cohort at 77 arches (not in Lean). The 78-arch witness is built around a 4-arch configuration the source draws as an example.

The mechanism is a short growth argument (marking a leaf multiplies the count by about n while an atom costs a constant factor), so a crossing had to occur; a strict reader might call the example a routine computation. The search for the crossing takes seconds.
